title: Foundries And OSATs Increasingly Overlap
gist: Foundries and OSATs are increasingly overlapping as foundry capacity constraints and fine-pitch advanced packaging push 2.5D, panel assembly and eventually hybrid bonding to OSATs, which are investing heavily (ASE spent $3.4B on equipment and raised its 2026 budget by 27%). Margin is shifting toward packaging and system integration, though OSATs' lower margins leave them more exposed to cycles.

insights.claim: Foundries and OSATs are blurring lanes as OSATs acquire select foundry capabilities and foundries return some work to OSATs, with the largest overlap in 2.5D integration and panel assembly and hybrid bonding likely to follow.
insights.speaker: Bryon Moyer
insights.so_what: Backend packaging revenue is migrating toward OSATs, affecting both OSAT and foundry mix.
insights.locator: Foundries and outsourced assembly and test

insights.claim: Zeiss's Raghu Nayak says IDMs and foundries are doing more of what OSATs can do while OSATs get closer to foundry back-end work.
insights.speaker: Bryon Moyer
insights.so_what: Equipment suppliers see demand from both sides of the convergence.

insights.claim: OSATs will never compete with foundries on advanced nodes and front-end wafer fabrication, but are replicating foundry capabilities for back-end activities where dimensions are less demanding.
insights.speaker: Bryon Moyer
insights.so_what: Limits the overlap to the back end; front-end moat of leading foundries is intact.
insights.locator: OSATs will never compete with foundries

insights.claim: Brewer Science reports lithography-related materials and processes are migrating from wafer fabs into advanced packaging environments as fine-pitch RDLs for AI, HBM and chiplets require wafer-fab-style patterning in packaging facilities.
insights.speaker: Bryon Moyer
insights.so_what: Materials and litho-equipment suppliers gain a packaging end market.
insights.quote: Advanced packaging is becoming more lithography-intensive,

insights.claim: Foundries cannot make all the chips clients want and are prioritizing newer-node silicon, likely turning away backend and legacy-process business, which spills to OSATs that share those lower-resolution capabilities.
insights.speaker: Bryon Moyer
insights.so_what: Foundry capacity tightness directly feeds OSAT utilization.
insights.locator: Foundries have been heavily involved in 2.5D packaging

insights.claim: EV Group's Thomas Uhrmann says with further volume restrictions both legacy-node and leading-edge products are shifting toward OSAT packaging.
insights.speaker: Bryon Moyer
insights.so_what: Spillover could extend from legacy to leading-edge products.
insights.quote: both legacy-node and leading-edge products are shifting toward OSAT packaging

insights.claim: Amkor says customers are asking whether it can attach electrical die to photonics die or wafer, dice the module and attach it to a substrate, which brings active alignment requirements for fiber attach and test.
insights.speaker: Bryon Moyer
insights.so_what: Photonics is a fast-growing demand source for OSAT 2.5D capability.

insights.claim: TSMC's move to panel-level packaging at 310 x 310 mm, closer to 300mm round-tool formats, let wafer-equipment makers scale up for high-performance materials and resolution rather than PCB equipment makers scaling down, whereas OSAT early lines targeted 500mm panels.
insights.speaker: Bryon Moyer
insights.so_what: TSMC's format choice steers equipment supplier winners toward wafer-tool vendors.

insights.claim: Hybrid bonding remains foundry and IDM dominated, and Uhrmann expects it to follow CoWoS: adoption at foundries, then OSATs as a second source once demand exceeds foundry capacity and processes mature.
insights.speaker: Bryon Moyer
insights.so_what: A future OSAT equipment cycle for hybrid bonding if demand outgrows foundry capacity.
insights.quote: We expect hybrid bonding to follow the same path as CoWoS
insights.locator: “We expect hybrid bonding to follow the same path as CoWoS

insights.claim: Heterogeneous integration sourcing dies from different technologies and suppliers, such as memory and photonics, may make OSAT participation in hybrid bonding more sensible than in vertically managed packages from one company.
insights.speaker: Bryon Moyer
insights.so_what: Multi-vendor chiplet ecosystems favor neutral third-party integrators.

insights.claim: Fortune Business Insights says advanced packaging grew to over $45B in 2025 and is expected to reach $100B by 2034, a CAGR just over 9%.
insights.speaker: Bryon Moyer
insights.so_what: Third-party sizing of the advanced packaging market for capex payback.
insights.locator: Fortune Business Insights says advanced packaging

insights.claim: ASE has already passed its $3.5 billion target for leading-edge packaging this year and expects to double it in 2027, according to EV Group's Uhrmann.
insights.speaker: Bryon Moyer
insights.so_what: Indicates the pace of OSAT leading-edge revenue growth.

insights.claim: Uhrmann argues margin is shifting from front-end manufacturing toward packaging and system integration because more system performance comes from advanced packaging, heterogeneous integration and 3D integration than from node scaling alone.
insights.speaker: Bryon Moyer
insights.so_what: Profit pool is migrating to packaging, a reason foundries want to retain it.
insights.quote: The margin is shifting from front-end chip manufacturing toward packaging and system integration

insights.claim: OSATs have structurally lower margins than foundries, so ROI depends on utilization and long-term customer commitments; currently OSATs are constrained by equipment lead times and cleanroom space rather than orders, so 2.5D, panel and test equipment investments pay back quickly.
insights.speaker: Bryon Moyer
insights.so_what: Near-term OSAT returns are strong but tied to overflow demand.

insights.claim: Because OSATs largely fill a spillover role, foundries win under most circumstances while OSATs may be more exposed to economic cycles as overflow demand comes and goes.
insights.speaker: Bryon Moyer
insights.so_what: Risk to OSAT earnings durability if foundry capacity loosens.
insights.locator: But if OSATs largely fulfill a spillover role

insights.claim: ASE spent $3.4B on equipment and raised its 2026 budget by 27%, then mid-year raised capital spend by another $1.5B, of which $600M is for equipment, per Seeking Alpha; Amkor is investing in a new Arizona facility.
insights.speaker: Bryon Moyer
insights.so_what: Capex signals demand for packaging equipment and materials suppliers.
insights.locator: All in all, OSATs are buying equipment
